name: Feast Of The New Moon The
overview: The Feast of the New Moon was a solemn monthly observance commanded by God, marked by specific burnt offerings and sacrifices as detailed in Numbers 28:11-15. These offerings included young bullocks, rams, lambs, and a kid goat for sin offerings, accompanied by flour and drink offerings, signifying a sweet savor unto the Lord. This feast was held on the first day of each month and involved worship in God's house, underscoring its importance in Israel's covenant relationship with God. However, the feast was not merely an outward ritual; it was meant to be a sincere act of worship, as mere external observance was hateful to God and condemned when practiced without true devotion.
